How this site was built, and what it does and does not cover
  • What it targets. Recurring examiner patterns across 8 past Research Methods II exams (LE1, LE2 and LE3 of the 2023, 2024 and 2025 batches), restricted to the 6 lectures in your LE2 coverage (RES2 2.01 to 2.06). Lectures 2.07 Data Presentation and 2.08 Writing the Research Proposal are excluded because they are not part of this LE2. Repeat families use every exam year. The All Questions tab carries the complete in-scope question set for 2024 and 2025 only, as you chose.
  • Sources. The 2023 LE1 was uploaded twice (identical files) and counted once. There is no 2024 LE1 in the project. LE3 2023 to 2025 were read from their project text because their PDFs were not attached. Page numbers for those three come from the page markers in that text.
  • Topics. One bucket per lecture trans in the project, assigned by the concept each item tests rather than the section it sat in. 338 extracted items belong to lectures that are not in the project and are left out of the families and the bank. They still appear in the Repeat Radar as "not covered here" so you can see what recurs outside your coverage:
    • Data Presentation (not in LE2 coverage): 2023 (16), 2024 (21), 2025 (20)
    • EBM and Critical Appraisal (not in project): 2023 (13), 2024 (21), 2025 (13)
    • Literature Review, Search, AI (not in project): 2023 (36), 2024 (5), 2025 (48)
    • Systematic Review and Meta-analysis (not in project): 2023 (15), 2024 (19), 2025 (19)
    • Writing the Introduction (not in project): 2023 (16), 2024 (3), 2025 (21)
    • Writing the Research Proposal (not in LE2 coverage): 2023 (15), 2024 (16), 2025 (21)
  • Same-year duplicates count once. When the same question appears twice in one year (for example an LE2 item recalled in that batch's LE3), it is shown once, under its earliest exam, with an "Also asked as" line. 85 such duplicate copies were merged. Different-year repeats stay separate because they show how the framing evolves.
  • Repeats. A family is one concept tested (keyed or central) in at least two different years. Families sort by number of appearances, then by how close the wording is. Distractor-only recurrences are listed in the Radar, never counted as repeats.
  • Keys. Every key is shown exactly as printed. Keys were confirmed by two methods (key column position and the item's own rationale, or the page image). 24 items carry an amber Source-key warning or cross-year discrepancy where the printed key conflicts with its rationale, the trans, or another year. Five 2025 LE3 items were empty templates in the source and are not included.
  • Rationales. Every choice of every family question and every bank question has its own rationale, built from the question's own feedback first, then other exam years, then the lecture trans. Where project sources cannot support a statement, the line says so. The Original PDF Rationale disclosure appears only where the raw text adds something.
  • Lecture Review column. Every repeat family and every 2024 to 2025 bank question has a lecture review built from the project trans, shown in the right-hand column of each family table and in a green panel under each bank question. Bank questions that belong to a family show that family's review. The Hide Lecture Review button hides them sitewide.
  • Hide Answers mode. A self-test mode, off when the page loads. It hides keys, the correct-choice highlight, rationales, rules, titles and reviews. Use Show or Reveal answer per question, click any blurred box to reveal just that box, or Reveal all answers in a family. Switching it off and on re-hides everything.
  • Coverage. All 68 families and all 214 bank questions are fully built. Radar rows marked "keyed in one year only" or "recurring distractor only" are concepts that recur without meeting the family threshold, not unbuilt families.
